Subject: Payment query: INV-2026-04 — intermediary bank fees

Hi Marissa,

We're ready to initiate the wire for INV-2026-04 (attached), but our treasury team flagged two items before we send:

1) Intermediary bank fees: Our bank (ANZ Sydney) says the SWIFT path to your USD account may route via an intermediary (HSBC London) and that intermediary fees are often deducted en route. Can you confirm whether Redwood expects the beneficiary (GlobalHealthTech) to bear any intermediary charges, or do you require "SHA" vs "OUR" routing?

2) Currency and FX: The invoice is USD. We operate in AUD and will likely ask our bank to perform FX. Is it acceptable if we pay in AUD and let our bank convert, or do you require USD-only wires to avoid revaluation on your side? If you accept AUD, please confirm your receiving currency details.

3) VAT/tax: This is an APAC entity — please confirm if any VAT/GST should be applied or if reverse-charge/self-assessment applies on your invoice.

We want to avoid short-payments due to fees being deducted. Attached is the invoice (INV-2026-04-GlobalHealthTech.pdf). Can you confirm the exact wire instructions and a recommended routing instruction we can hand to ANZ?

Thanks,

Hi Asha — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the invoice. Looping in Michael (finance) and Rishi (AE) to ensure we give you the cleanest instructions. A few quick points while Michael confirms the bank text below:

- Preferred: USD wire with OUR charges (beneficiary covers no intermediary deductions).
- If your bank cannot send OUR, SHA is tolerable but you will likely see intermediary deductions; we then ask that you either instruct ANZ to cover ALL fees or provide proof of the full amount reaching our account so we can reconcile.
- We are fine if you pay in AUD, but to avoid reconciliation mismatches we prefer USD. If you must pay AUD, please confirm the FX rate applied (or allow us to apply the rate on receipt) and include a SWIFT message with beneficiary reference: INV-2026-04 / GlobalHealthTech.

Michael — can you paste Redwood's current wire block and specify the fields for intermediary bank routing? Also confirm whether VAT/GST applies for GlobalHealthTech (APAC entity).

Hi Asha — thanks, and sorry for the delay. Below is the full wire instruction block we publish for international USD wires. Please hand this exact block to ANZ and request either OUR or specify "BENEFICIARY ACCOUNT must receive full USD amount (no intermediary deductions)" in the SWIFT message text.

Redwood Inference — USD Account (correspondence / intermediary may apply)
Bank name: First Redwood Bank (US fictional)
Bank address: 100 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94105, USA
SWIFT/BIC: FRRDUS6S
Account name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
Account number (USD): 987654321
ABA (routing): 121000089
Beneficiary reference: INV-2026-04 / GlobalHealthTech

Intermediary clarification: if your bank routes via an intermediary (example: HSBC London), intermediary fees can be deducted by that intermediary unless the sending bank sets the charge type to OUR. If ANZ cannot do OUR, please instruct them to reimburse any intermediary fees to your payables contact and include the intermediary fee amount on the remittance advice. We will accept the payment and then reconcile; if there is a short payment we will coordinate promptly once you provide the remittance and SWIFT MT103 copy.

Currency handling: Redwood invoices are issued in USD. We prefer USD wires. If you instruct AUD payment (bank-side FX), include the FX details on remittance (rate and originating bank charge). We do not apply VAT on Redwood-hosted services for APAC corporate customers where reverse-charge rules apply — however, this depends on your local tax position. For GlobalHealthTech (APAC entity), if you are registered for GST in Australia, reverse-charge/self-assessment likely applies; if not, standard local GST may be required. We recommend you consult your tax advisor.

Attachments: same wire block (Redwood_wire_instructions_2026Q2.pdf).

If you'd like, we can propose a payment alternative via our USD ACH/Payoneer partner for lower intermediary exposure — Rishi, Dev, can you add a quick note on alternatives?
